sources.verified_claim: SBA 7(a) is a loan guarantee to participating lenders; SBA-backed financing can fund working capital, equipment, real estate and ownership changes. The federal lender guarantee is distinct from an owner personal guarantee.
13 CFR 120.160, eCFR current through October 15, 2026: holders of at least 20 percent ownership generally must guarantee SBA business loans; SBA or lender may require other appropriate guarantors.
SBA Form 148 page says owners of 20 percent or more must provide an unlimited personal guaranty; lenders may use this SBA form. Actual signed terms govern a particular obligation.

SBA SOP 50 10 governs origination of 7(a) and 504 loans. Version 8.1 with technical updates is effective October 1, 2026; article avoids asserting a case-specific loan term from the generic program description.
2026 report on 2025 weighted convenience sample says 59 percent of indebted respondent firms used a personal guarantee; it is not a random national prevalence estimate.

visual_text_rule: No requested labels, numbers, scales, chart values or readable writing. Images qualitatively distinguish the SBA lender guarantee from the owner guarantee and show a conditional default exposure path. Unexpected visible text must be checked against sources or rejected.
